bugs.title: Edit task modal (#modal-edit) renders on page load without "hidden" class, blocking all interaction with the task list
bugs.root_cause:
The #modal-edit div in the initial HTML lacks the 'hidden' class, so it renders as a full-viewport fixed overlay from page load (Evaluate confirms: classList='modal', hasHidden=false, display='flex', position='fixed', zIndex='50', 1280×720 at top:0 left:0).
Because the overlay covers the entire viewport at z-index:50 with position:fixed, it intercepts all pointer events on the task list beneath it. InspectElement confirms #modal-edit obstructs the center point of #task-list.
Playwright's click on the first task's Edit button (selector: #task-list > li:nth-of-type(1) > button:nth-of-type(1)) times out after 15000ms with 29 retry attempts, each reporting '#modal-edit intercepts pointer events'.
repro: 2. Open the edit modal for the first task in the list by clicking its edit button

raw.description: The #modal-edit dialog div in the initial HTML lacks the "hidden" class, so it is rendered as a full-viewport fixed overlay (position:fixed, z-index:50, 1280×720, display:flex, visibility:visible, opacity:1) from the moment the page loads. This invisible-to-the-user overlay intercepts every pointer event on the underlying task list, making it impossible to click any task's Edit button. The openEdit function (app.js line 175) removes "hidden" to show the modal, and closeModal (line 263) adds "hidden" to hide it — but since the initial HTML never includes "hidden", the modal is active immediately on page load without any user action.

bugs.title: Toast overlay #toast covers and intercepts #btn-settings button
bugs.root_cause: The #toast overlay with position:fixed and z-index:90 renders at rect (1068,14,1266,56), directly over the #btn-settings button at rect (1177,14,1258,52). Because the toast has higher z-index and is painted on top, document.elementFromPoint at the overlap centroid (1218,33) returns #toast instead of the button, making the Settings button unclickable while the toast is visible.

raw.description: A welcome-back toast notification (position: fixed, z-index: 90) overlaps the Settings button in the top-right area, covering it entirely and intercepting clicks so the user cannot interact with Settings while the toast is visible.

bugs.title: Tab buttons with role="tab" never set aria-selected, violating WCAG 4.1.2
bugs.root_cause:
The filter buttons use role="tab" inside a role="tablist" section, establishing them as ARIA tabs that require aria-selected per the WAI-ARIA tab pattern.
Evaluating all three tab buttons at the end of the recording confirms none have aria-selected set — all return null/false.
The source code shows the click handler only toggles 'is-active' CSS class and never sets aria-selected, confirming the attribute is never managed programmatically.

raw.description: On route /tasker-fixture/, filter buttons use role="tab" inside a role="tablist" container. The active tab ("All") has a visual "is-active" class but no aria-selected attribute is ever set on any tab. Screen readers and other assistive technology cannot determine which tab is selected, violating WCAG 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value).
